candidates.exact_span: Results of a ground-water monitoring program developed by a qualified ground-water scientist, or a certification by a qualified ground-water scientist may be used to demonstrate that sewage sludge placed on an active sewage sludge unit does not contaminate an aquifer.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The disjunctive 'monitoring program ... or a certification' determines whether groundwater monitoring is an applicable obligation versus a certification-only demonstration path; a different reading of which option applies changes whether missing groundwater monitoring data is a required-monitoring gap (C) or a satisfied alternative (C), and whether monitoring was required at all (B).

candidates.exact_span: A description of how either the Class A or Class B pathogen reduction requirements are met or whether sewage sludge placed on a surface disposal site is covered with soil or other material at the end of each operating day.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpretation of which branch applies (Class A, Class B, or daily soil/material cover for surface disposal) changes which pathogen-related monitoring and management obligations are in force for the facility (B).

candidates.exact_span: A description of how the vector attraction reduction requirements are met.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Which vector attraction reduction method is documented as met determines the applicable vector-attraction monitoring and compliance pathway tied to later DMR reporting of the chosen alternative (B).

candidates.exact_span: Report YES for liner and leachate collection system at surface disposal site.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether this affirmative DMR reporting item is an operative monitoring/reporting obligation for the permittee's surface disposal configuration affects whether a missing or negative response is treated as required evidence not provided (C) versus not applicable (B/C).

candidates.exact_span: The frequency of monitoring listed in Element 2, Section I.D. which applies to the permittee.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The cross-reference to Element 2, Section I.D. and the qualifier 'which applies to the permittee' govern which monitoring frequencies are actually binding; different readings of applicability change the set of required monitoring periods and events (B).

TCLP Pass/Fail is a compliance-oriented reported result that may be compared to an enforceable pass standard (A), establishes a monitoring/reporting duty (B), and requires distinguishing documented pass/fail from missing or non-comparable evidence (C).

candidates.exact_span: The concentration (mg/Kg ) in the sludge of PCBs.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Reported PCB concentration in mg/Kg is a numeric parameter subject to limit comparison (A) and implies an applicable monitoring and annual reporting obligation for that parameter (B).

candidates.exact_span: Level of pathogen reduction achieved (C lass A or Class B), unless Vector attraction reduction alternative no. 11 is used.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The exception 'unless Vector attraction reduction alternative no. 11 is used' makes pathogen-level DMR reporting conditionally required; whether alternative 11 applies changes if missing pathogen-level data means monitoring was not required (C) or required evidence is absent (C), and alters applicable reporting obligations (B).

candidates.exact_span: List Alternative used as listed in Section I.C.3.(a. or b.). Alternatives describe how the pathogen reduction requirements are met.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Which Section I.C.3.(a. or b.) alternative is selected determines the operative pathogen-reduction compliance pathway and associated monitoring or demonstration requirements (B).

candidates.exact_span: Vector attraction reduction Alternative used as listed in Section I.B.4. h.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Identification of the Section I.B.4.h alternative (including whether alternative 11 is used) changes which vector-attraction and related conditional reporting obligations apply, affecting both required monitoring (B) and how missing related results are classified (C).

candidates.exact_span: Annual sludge production in dry metric tons/year.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether nonzero annual sludge production establishes that sludge management and associated monitoring/reporting duties were triggered during the period affects applicability of sludge-related obligations (B) and whether absent data reflects no activity versus missing required reporting (C).

candidates.exact_span: Amount of sludge surface disposed in dry metric tons/year.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Reported surface disposal quantity bears on whether surface-disposal-specific monitoring and reporting requirements (liner/leachate, groundwater, pathogen/vector items) were operative in the period (B) and whether missing related evidence indicates no discharge versus inadequate documentation (C).

candidates.exact_span: A narrative description explaining how the management practices in §503.24 are met shall be attached to the DMR.
candidates.computation_change_reason: This attached narrative is a distinct annual reporting obligation; interpretation of whether §503.24 management-practice demonstration is required for the permittee's activities affects monitoring/reporting applicability (B) and whether a missing attachment is unresolved missing evidence or not required (C).

candidates.exact_span: A certification statement that all applicable requirements (specifically listed) have been met, and that the permittee understands that there are significant penalties for false certification including fine and imprisonment (See 503.27(a)(1)(ii) or 503.27(a)(2)(ii) whichever applies to the permittees sludge disposal activities) shall be attached to the DMR.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The choice between 503.27(a)(1)(ii) and 503.27(a)(2)(ii) 'whichever applies' and which requirements are 'specifically listed' change which certification form is operative for the permittee's sludge disposal mode; misclassification alters whether a missing DMR attachment is a required reporting element (B) or a different no-data state (C).
